international.canonicalTopic: New Zealand parliamentary approval of India–New Zealand FTA legislation
international.headline: New Zealand Parliament approves legislation for India–New Zealand FTA
facts: New Zealand’s Parliament approved legislation to implement the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement on 2026-09-16, completing a legislative step for implementation.
The agreement was signed in New Delhi in April 2026 after negotiations concluded within a year.
The stated aim is to double bilateral trade to USD 5 billion within five years.
An FTA seeks to reduce or eliminate tariffs and other trade barriers across areas such as goods, services, investment and market access.
international.summary: New Zealand’s parliamentary approval advanced the domestic legislative process for implementing the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement.
international.staticLink: A free trade agreement reduces or removes trade barriers to support trade and economic integration.
international.prelimsTakeaway: New Zealand parliamentary approval was dated 2026-09-16; the agreement’s stated objective is to double bilateral trade to USD 5 billion within five years.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how free trade agreements can expand market access while requiring attention to domestic competitiveness and implementation.

sources.title: New Zealand Parliament Approves India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement

international.notes:
# 1. Parliamentary approval
- **What:** **New Zealand’s Parliament** approved legislation to implement the **India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA)**
- **When:** **16 September 2026**
- **Status:** **APPROVED**; a legislative step towards implementation, not confirmation that implementation is complete

# 2. Agreement facts
- **Signed:** **New Delhi**, **April 2026**
- **Negotiations:** Concluded within **one year**
- **Objective:** Double bilateral trade to **USD 5 billion** within **five years**
- **FTA:** Agreement seeking to reduce or eliminate tariffs and other trade barriers across **goods, services, investment and market access**
- ⚠ **Trap:** Parliamentary approval of implementing legislation is a step in the process; it does not mean the FTA has already been fully implemented
# 3. Also note
- New Zealand’s Parliament approved legislation to implement the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement on 2026-09-16, completing a legislative step for implementation.
> Exam angle: Test the approval date, stated trade target and distinction between a legislative step and completed implementation.

international.headline: BIMSTEC traditional medicine conference takes place in Goa
facts: The 3rd BIMSTEC Conference on Traditional Medicine Knowledge, Genetic Resources and Intellectual Property Rights was held in Goa on September 16–17, 2026.
The Ministry of Ayush organised the conference, with the All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa, as the nodal institution.
The 2nd BIMSTEC Nodal Group meeting on Traditional Medicine Knowledge, Genetic Resources and Intellectual Property Rights took place alongside it.
BIMSTEC has seven members: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand; its headquarters are in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
international.summary: The conference brought BIMSTEC participants together to discuss traditional medicine knowledge, genetic resources and intellectual property rights.
international.staticLink: BIMSTEC was established in 1997; its full name is Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The conference was held in Goa and organised by the Ministry of Ayush with AIIA Goa as the nodal institution.
international.mainsAngle: Examine the governance challenges around traditional knowledge, genetic resources and intellectual property in regional cooperation.
international.apLink: The conference was held in Goa, India; no AP-specific connection is stated.

international.canonicalTopic: Hashim Thaçi Kosovo Specialist Chambers sentence
international.headline: Hashim Thaçi sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
facts: The Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague sentenced former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi to 25 years in prison on 16 September 2026 for war crimes linked to the 1998–99 Kosovo conflict.
The notes list convictions for murder, torture, cruel treatment and unlawful or arbitrary detention; they state that six charges relating to crimes against humanity were dismissed.
The court found him responsible for 96 murders, 385 unlawful detentions, torture of 303 people and cruel treatment of 49 people not participating in the conflict.
The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was established in 2015 and is seated in The Hague.
international.summary: The Kosovo Specialist Chambers issued a 25-year sentence against former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi for war crimes arising from the Kosovo conflict.
international.staticLink: The Kosovo Specialist Chambers is a Kosovo court staffed by international judges and personnel, with its seat in The Hague.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The sentence was issued on 16 September 2026 by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague.
international.mainsAngle: Examine the role of specialised internationalised courts in accountability for crimes committed during conflict.

sources.title: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaçi Sentenced to 25 Years for War Crimes

international.notes:
# 1. Judgement
- **Court:** **Kosovo Specialist Chambers**, seated in **The Hague**
- **When:** **16 September 2026**
- **Outcome:** **Hashim Thaçi** sentenced to **25 years in prison** for war crimes linked to the **1998–99 Kosovo conflict**
- **Status:** **FINAL_RESULT**

# 2. Case facts
- **Person:** **Hashim Thaçi**, former **President of Kosovo**
- **Convictions listed:** **Murder, torture, cruel treatment, and unlawful or arbitrary detention**
- **Dismissed charges:** **Six** charges relating to crimes against humanity
| Finding | Number |
|---|---:|
| **Murders** | **96** |
| **Unlawful detentions** | **385** |
| **People tortured** | **303** |
| **People subjected to cruel treatment, not participating in the conflict** | **49** |

# 3. Court background
- **Established:** **2015**
- **Seat:** **The Hague**
- **Composition:** Kosovo court staffed by **international judges and personnel**
- ⚠ **Trap:** The **25-year sentence** concerns war crimes linked to the Kosovo conflict; the notes state that **six crimes-against-humanity charges were dismissed**

> Exam angle: Identify Hashim Thaçi’s former office, the sentencing court and seat, and the distinction between convictions listed and dismissed charges.

international.headline: World Ozone Day highlights global action to protect the ozone layer
facts: World Ozone Day is observed on September 16; the notes give 1994 as the starting year.
The 2026 theme is “Global Action for a Cooler Planet”.
The notes associate it with UNEP and the UN General Assembly and link the observance to the 1987 signing of the Montreal Protocol.
international.summary: The observance draws attention to international efforts to protect the ozone layer and the Montreal Protocol.
international.prelimsTakeaway: World Ozone Day is September 16; the notes list the 2026 theme as “Global Action for a Cooler Planet”.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the significance of international cooperation and the Montreal Protocol in environmental protection.
international.notes:
# 1. Observance
- **What:** **World Ozone Day**
- **Date:** **16 September**
- **First observed / starting year:** **1994**
- **2026 theme:** **“Global Action for a Cooler Planet”**
- **Observed by / associated with:** **UNEP** and the **United Nations General Assembly**
- **Status:** **ONGOING**

# 2. Ozone protection
- **Related agreement:** **Montreal Protocol**
- **Protocol milestone:** Signed in **1987**
- ⚠ **Trap:** **World Ozone Day** is observed on **16 September**; the **Montreal Protocol** is the related international agreement, signed in **1987**

> Exam angle: Recall World Ozone Day’s date and 2026 theme, and connect the observance with the Montreal Protocol.

national.canonicalTopic: Shehzad Bhatti Network designated under UAPA
national.headline: Shehzad Bhatti Network listed as 46th terrorist organisation under UAPA
facts: The Ministry of Home Affairs declared the Pakistan-based Shehzad Bhatti Network a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, on September 16, 2026.
It was listed as the 46th terrorist organisation in the Act’s First Schedule under Section 35(1)(a).
Section 35 empowers the Central Government to add or remove organisations from the First Schedule as terrorist organisations.

The notes attribute to the Ministry of Home Affairs allegations of arms, explosives and narcotics smuggling, radicalisation, resource mobilisation for unlawful activity and dissemination of provocative digital content.
national.summary: The Shehzad Bhatti Network was added to the UAPA First Schedule as the 46th designated terrorist organisation.
national.staticLink: The UAPA, enacted in 1967, is administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs; Section 35 concerns listing organisations in the First Schedule.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The listing was made under Section 35(1)(a) of the UAPA.
national.mainsAngle: The designation illustrates the statutory framework for responding to organisations identified as threats to national security.

sources.title: Shehzad Bhatti Network Declared 46th Terrorist Organisation under UAPA

national.notes:

- **What:** The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** declared the **Pakistan-based Shehzad Bhatti Network** a terrorist organisation under the **Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (UAPA)**.
- **When:** **September 16, 2026**
- **Status:** **Completed**
- **AP link:** No direct **Andhra Pradesh**-specific link established.

# 2. Listing and legal basis
- **Listing:** **46th terrorist organisation** in the UAPA’s **First Schedule**
- **Section:** **Section 35(1)(a)**
- **Authority:** **Section 35** empowers the **Central Government** to add or remove organisations from the **First Schedule** as terrorist organisations. [GK]
- **Background:** The **UAPA** was enacted in **1967** and is administered by the **Ministry of Home Affairs**. [GK]
- ⚠ **Trap:** The listing concerns an **organisation**, not an individual; the stated provision is **Section 35(1)(a)**.

national.headline: India’s 51st Doppler Weather Radar is inaugurated in Odisha
facts: A Doppler Weather Radar was inaugurated at Jamadarpali in Sambalpur, Odisha, on September 16, 2026, under Mission Mausam.
The notes identify it as India’s 51st radar and Odisha’s third, after Paradip and Gopalpur; it is described as a Make in India system.
It has a stated coverage radius of 250 km, a resolution of 150 metres and updates weather information every 10 minutes.
The radar supports short-term weather monitoring, storm tracking and rainfall estimation; the notes state that another 40–50 radars are planned under Mission Mausam.
Mission Mausam was approved in 2024, has an outlay of ₹2,000 crore and is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
national.summary: The Sambalpur radar adds to India’s weather-observation network and is intended to support local monitoring of storms, precipitation and rainfall.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The radar was inaugurated at Jamadarpali, Sambalpur; the notes give a 250-km radius, 150-metre resolution and 10-minute updates.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how improved observation systems can strengthen early warning, short-term forecasting and disaster preparedness.
